answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it can enter a task market, then slash that stake when independent, randomly assigned reviewers confirm fraud or coordinated duplicate behavior. Sybils cannot gain influence merely by multiplying accounts: each new identity ties up more capital, while colluding accounts risk losing it. A participant named onyx might review willow’s work while falcon audits the dispute, but the protection depends on costly, verifiable bonds and unbiased review—not names alone.
